sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: brake failure by transmission, wet brakes versus long hills, blowouts versus flats, skids, rear impacts and crash duties
Confusable pairs among the emergency procedures and post-crash duties, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
With failed brakes, a manual car downshifts and releases the clutch before the emergency brake, while an automatic applies the emergency brake and selects low range. [A01]
Why it matters: group brake failure; difficulty medium; confusable manual versus automatic.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Wet brakes are dried with light brake pressure over a short drive, while a long downhill calls for a lower gear instead of the brake pedal. [A01]
Why it matters: group brakes; difficulty medium; confusable using versus sparing the brakes.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
A stuck gas pedal calls for shifting to neutral and braking firmly, whereas brake failure calls for a lower gear and the emergency brake. [A01]
Why it matters: group pedal emergencies; difficulty high; confusable stuck throttle versus failed brakes.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A02
During a blowout you hold the wheel straight and avoid braking until the engine slows the car, while a flat tire change starts only once the car is fully off the road. [A02]
Why it matters: group tires; difficulty medium; confusable driving response versus stopped procedure.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A02
A breakdown signal for help is a white cloth on the left door handle or aerial plus a raised hood, and everyone exits on the passenger side. [A02]
Why it matters: group breakdowns; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A03
Running onto the shoulder means no hard braking and no sharp turn back, while an oncoming car in your lane means keep right even off the road. [A03]
Why it matters: group off-road; difficulty medium; confusable shoulder recovery versus head-on avoidance.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A03
In a skid you first steer toward the rear's slide and then steer back as the car straightens, so the two steering moves happen in sequence. [A03]
Why it matters: group skids; difficulty high; misconception target.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A03
With ABS you hold firm steady pressure to avoid a skid, but without ABS you pump the brakes gently. [A03]
Why it matters: group skids; difficulty high; confusable ABS versus non-ABS braking.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A03
If a rear impact is coming and the road ahead is clear you accelerate away, but you also brace and press your head against the head rest. [A03]
Why it matters: group crash avoidance; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A04
A crash must be reported to police right away for any death or injury, or for apparent damage of $1,000 or more, while reporting to your insurer is advised for every crash. [A04]
Why it matters: group crash duties; difficulty high; confusable police report versus insurer report.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]
